bookmarks.title: Margin Note Market Character Bookmark
bookmarks.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper bookmark for older writers to build a character from one kind note and one clearer choice.
bookmarks.adultSetup: Print one bookmark strip, set out pencils and blank paper, and invite the writer to imagine a pretend market where every stall trades helpful story notes.
bookmarks.kidDirection: Invent a character who receives one margin note, then show how the note changes what the character chooses next.
bookmarks.bookmarkFrontPrompt: Front prompt: My character arrives at Margin Note Market carrying a note that says ____________________.
bookmarks.bookmarkBackPrompt: Back prompt: The note changes the character's next choice by making them ____________________.
bookmarks.storySeedPrompt: Story seed: A careful note trader gives the character one question that changes the scene: ____________________.
bookmarks.firstLinePath: First-line path: The character wanted ____________________, but the market note pointed toward ____________________.
bookmarks.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one visible habit, gesture, or object that shows the character's choice: ____________________.
bookmarks.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the character's changed choice on the bookmark back: ____________________.
bookmarks.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use this bookmark later to start a character scene about ____________________.

bookmarks.title: Binding Day Boardwalk Sequence Bookmark
bookmarks.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper bookmark for arranging a short creative story into a clear first, next, and final moment.
bookmarks.adultSetup: Print one bookmark strip, place pencils and scrap paper nearby, and ask the writer to picture a bright boardwalk where blank pages wait in order.
bookmarks.kidDirection: Choose three page moments for a pretend boardwalk story, then write the order that makes the ending feel earned.
bookmarks.bookmarkFrontPrompt: Front prompt: The first boardwalk page shows ____________________, and the next page must explain ____________________.
bookmarks.bookmarkBackPrompt: Back prompt: My final page belongs after ____________________ because ____________________.
bookmarks.storySeedPrompt: Story seed: A finished booklet feels out of order until one page clue reveals ____________________.
bookmarks.firstLinePath: First-line path: First ____________________; next ____________________; finally the boardwalk page lands on ____________________.
bookmarks.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add a bridge sentence that explains why one moment follows the last: ____________________.
bookmarks.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Number three tiny page ideas, then write only the middle turn: ____________________.
bookmarks.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use the final page clue to polish a tiny ending about ____________________.

bookmarks.title: Index Card Theater Character Bookmark
bookmarks.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper bookmark for creating a character through two short lines, one stage cue, and one changed choice.
bookmarks.adultSetup: Print one bookmark strip, set out paper and pencils, and invite the writer to imagine a tiny tabletop theater built from blank index cards.
bookmarks.kidDirection: Give one character a goal, write two short lines, and let the second line change what the character decides to do.
bookmarks.bookmarkFrontPrompt: Front prompt: My character steps onto the index-card stage wanting ____________________.
bookmarks.bookmarkBackPrompt: Back prompt: The stage cue that changes the character's choice is ____________________.
bookmarks.storySeedPrompt: Story seed: Two index cards create a scene when one character quietly decides ____________________.
bookmarks.firstLinePath: First-line path: The first line says ____________________; the reply reveals ____________________; the choice turns toward ____________________.
bookmarks.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace one explanation with an action the reader can see on the paper stage: ____________________.
bookmarks.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the two spoken lines, then underline the line that changes the choice: ____________________.
bookmarks.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use the clearest stage cue to begin a short scene about ____________________.

bookmarks.title: Clue Label Tower Sensory Bookmark
bookmarks.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper bookmark for collecting concrete color, sound, texture, and shape details for an invented museum scene.
bookmarks.adultSetup: Print one bookmark strip, provide pencils and blank paper, and ask the writer to imagine a quiet tower museum filled with unlabeled ordinary clues.
bookmarks.kidDirection: Invent one exhibit label, then choose sensory details that help a reader picture the clue without needing a real place or real object name.
bookmarks.bookmarkFrontPrompt: Front prompt: The tower label names an exhibit shaped like ____________________.
bookmarks.bookmarkBackPrompt: Back prompt: The exhibit has a color ____________________, a texture ____________________, and a quiet sound ____________________.
bookmarks.storySeedPrompt: Story seed: A museum helper notices one tiny label clue that points toward ____________________.
bookmarks.firstLinePath: First-line path: The label looks like ____________________; the room feels ____________________; the clue suggests ____________________.
bookmarks.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace one plain describing word with a sharper sensory detail: ____________________.
bookmarks.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Sketch the label first, then write one sensory sentence here: ____________________.
bookmarks.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use this label later to build a quiet tower scene about ____________________.

bookmarks.title: Revision River Ferry Bookmark
bookmarks.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper bookmark for revising a short ending by bringing back one earlier clue with clearer wording.
bookmarks.adultSetup: Print one bookmark strip, set out pencils and paper, and invite the writer to imagine a calm ferry carrying draft sentences across a river of blank pages.
bookmarks.kidDirection: Pick one earlier story clue, draft a final sentence, and revise the ending so the clue returns in a clearer way.
bookmarks.bookmarkFrontPrompt: Front prompt: The earlier story clue I want to bring back is ____________________.
bookmarks.bookmarkBackPrompt: Back prompt: My revised final sentence carries that clue across the river by saying ____________________.
bookmarks.storySeedPrompt: Story seed: A ferry guide finds an old draft clue floating beside ____________________.
bookmarks.firstLinePath: First-line path: At the beginning, the clue was ____________________; near the ferry, it returns as ____________________.
bookmarks.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Trim one extra phrase or add one clearer ending image: ____________________.
bookmarks.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle one final sentence on paper, then copy the revised version here: ____________________.
bookmarks.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use this revised ending to finish a tiny story about ____________________.
